section_summary: This section documents efforts to discourage credit to Japanese interests, including a proposed machinery sale and Australian wheat transactions. It also covers Japanese budget reductions, possible withdrawals of Japanese funds from American banks, and FBI tracking of Japanese banking and organizational accounts in New York. The final FBI report continues beyond page 159.

subfiles.title: FBI letter correcting recipient of transferred funds
subfiles.about: Corrects the reported identity of a recipient of Italian-Japanese funds and mentions Swiss Bank transfers.
subfiles.summary: The FBI identifies Hideo Itoh as the intended recipient of a secret cash delivery and reports further inquiry.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Italian-Japanese funds
subfiles.about: Acknowledges two FBI letters and requests further information.
subfiles.summary: Berle thanks Hoover and asks for updates on the fund transfers.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation with Ferdinand Thun
subfiles.about: Records an oral warning against extending credit for machinery sold to Japanese silk interests.
subfiles.summary: After consulting Hornbeck, the writer told Thun the Department hoped no credit would be extended and asked that its involvement remain private.

subfiles.title: Suggested response to Textile Machine Works
subfiles.about: Drafts talking points discouraging credit for Japanese purchase of knitting machinery.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum links the proposed purchase to Japanese control of central China's silk trade and cites exchange risks and injury to American interests.

subfiles.title: Textile Machine Works request for advice
subfiles.about: Asks for policy advice on selling used knitting machines on credit to Gunze Silk Corp.
subfiles.summary: Thun describes planned installation near Shanghai and asks whether to continue negotiations.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Mitsui bills of exchange
subfiles.about: Reports Mitsui's discounted bills and possible planned spending.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports $200,000 in bills discounted at Bank of America and a possible $320,000–$350,000 expenditure.

subfiles.title: Savings in the 1940–1941 Japanese budget
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Analyzes announced reductions of ¥645,187,000 in Japanese government expenditure.
subfiles.summary: The report separates cancelled and postponed appropriations, removes duplicate transfers, and calculates a revised budget of ¥9,912,154,434. It notes cuts to civilian programs and no reductions in military expenditures.

subfiles.title: Reported Australian flour and wheat sales
subfiles.about: Recommends verifying credit terms reportedly offered for Australian grain sales to Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Becker relayed a Mitsubishi representative's account of half cash and half four-month credit terms.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Canberra about Australian wheat sale
subfiles.about: Requests verification of an Australian wheat sale and comparison with earlier Japanese purchases.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Canberra to verify quantity, purchaser, payment schedule, and interest.

subfiles.title: Note on Canberra's wheat-credit report
subfiles.about: Interprets Canberra's report on Australia's limited short-term wheat credit.
subfiles.summary: The note says Australian censorship delays prompted a final, less generous credit exception.

subfiles.title: Canberra telegram on wheat-credit terms
subfiles.about: Confirms the wheat transaction and explains its exception to Australia's cash-sales policy.
subfiles.summary: Gauss reports that earlier credits ran 12–18 months, while censorship delays influenced the new short-term exception.

subfiles.title: British ban on new credits to Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Records British Embassy notice of a ban on new export credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Stopford offers to obtain details of particular credits from London.

subfiles.title: Australian credits for wheat and flour
subfiles.doc_type: despatch with enclosed memorandum of conversation
subfiles.about: Reports Australian officials' intention to avoid further wheat and flour credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Gauss encloses Minter's conversation with Murphy, who describes earlier 12–18 month credit terms and says new credits are unlikely. Murphy also reports investigation of an unfounded claim that American official guarantees supported wheat shipments to Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Canberra despatches
subfiles.about: Forwards two Canberra despatches on Australian grain credits.
subfiles.summary: Transmits despatches 34 and 45 for the Agriculture Secretary's information.

subfiles.title: Tokyo warning of Japanese dollar withdrawals
subfiles.about: Warns that Japanese commercial dollar credits may be moved from American banks to finance German trade.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports German demands for advance payment, possible transfer routes through firms in several countries, and Japanese changes to export-bill settlement for Sweden. He urges attention to American assets frozen in Japan.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo withdrawal warning
subfiles.about: Restates the warning about Japanese dollar withdrawals and German trade financing.
subfiles.summary: This paraphrase repeats the proposed transfer routes, changes to Swedish export bills, and concern over American credits frozen in Japan.

subfiles.title: Response to Tokyo on dollar credits
subfiles.about: Addresses possible restrictions on Japanese dollar holdings and American funds frozen in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department says it has no general exchange control or clearing arrangement and proposes a separate approach to Japan's Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Tokyo telegram to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards a paraphrase of the Tokyo telegram on recent Japanese financial developments.
subfiles.summary: Sends Treasury a copy of Tokyo telegram 1150.

subfiles.title: Canberra despatch 45 on wheat credits
subfiles.doc_type: despatch with enclosed memorandum of conversation
subfiles.about: Clarifies the Australian wheat sale and identifies Mitsui as purchaser.
subfiles.summary: Minter's enclosed account says Mitsui received a brief extension to an expired option because Australian censorship had delayed its instructions. Murphy denies that Mitsubishi bought the wheat, confirms 4½ percent interest, and says Australia intended no further such transactions.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Canberra despatch 45
subfiles.about: Repeats the despatch and conversation memorandum identifying Mitsui as the Australian wheat purchaser.
subfiles.summary: This filed copy repeats the explanation of the expired option, censorship delay, short-term credit, and Murphy's denial of a Mitsubishi purchase.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Japanese gold shipment
subfiles.about: Traces a Japanese gold shipment from Kobe through the San Francisco Mint into New York banking accounts.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports the sale of 89,128 fine ounces and subsequent transfer of about $3 million to New York.

subfiles.title: FBI report on bonds and bank transactions
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese bond shipment, Mitsui instructions, and large bank transactions.
subfiles.summary: The letter notes bonds sent toward Japan, Mitsui's instruction to reduce commitments, and separate Treasury-bill and bank transfers.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal of Japanese funds reports
subfiles.about: Sends three FBI reports concerning Japanese funds.
subfiles.summary: Encloses reports dated October 15, October 29, and November 13.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Japanese accounts through October 31
subfiles.from: N. Frankel, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Analyzes October deposits and withdrawals in Japanese consular, commercial, and cultural-organization bank accounts.
subfiles.summary: The report follows funds through the Japanese Consulate General, Japan Institute, Showa Tsusho Kaisha, H. Itoh's account, and the Japanese Association of New York. It lists checks, transfers, letters of credit, and balances at Chase National Bank and National City Bank. Investigators identify substantial flows among Japanese firms and banks and plan to keep monitoring the accounts.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Japanese accounts through October 15
subfiles.from: N. Frankel, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Examines Showa Tsusho Kaisha, Japan Institute, and Japanese consular accounts in early October.
subfiles.summary: The report details the closure of Showa Tsusho Kaisha's special account and transfer to an account under H. Itoh's name, along with payments to Japanese firms and Bangkok. It traces Japan Institute funding from the Consulate General, describes its predecessor and officers, and itemizes consular-account checks. The report continues beyond page 159.
